previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of stroke with right-sided weakness, was admitted for right upper extremity swelling, pain, and erythema. Evaluation revealed a MRSA-positive abscess in the distal forearm and a thrombus in the cephalic vein, likely related to a recent peripheral IV. He underwent two incision and drainage procedures and was treated with a 7-day course of vancomycin adjusted for dialysis. Imaging showed chronic occlusion of the superior vena cava near a prior stent, with collateral drainage; attempts to recannulate were unsuccessful, and a repeat procedure under general anesthesia was scheduled as an outpatient. Incidental findings included a large left thyroid mass and a right adrenal mass, both requiring non-emergent follow-up imaging. The patient improved clinically, with reduced swelling and pain, and was discharged to extended care with instructions for wound care, antibiotic completion, premedication for contrast, and follow-up on the imaging findings.
problems: MRSA abscess of right upper extremity

Left-sided dual lumen subclavian central venous catheter tip terminates within
the proximal right atrium, coursing through a vascular stent within the left
brachiocephalic vein and superior vena cava.  Cardiac silhouette size is
normal.  Mild rightward deviation of the trachea with left superior
mediastinal mass compatible with a known thyroid goiter is unchanged. Hilar
contours are unchanged.  Pulmonary vasculature is not engorged.  Subsegmental
atelectasis is noted in the lung bases without focal consolidation.  No
pleural effusion or pneumothorax is demonstrated.  Marked degenerative changes
of the left glenohumeral joints and remote right posterior rib are re-
demonstrated.
